title: Access control by role, by attribute and by row or column

videos.script: Bruno is an analyst. He needs to count customers by state. Carla works in support. She needs the names and addresses of the customers she answers, and only those. {{two}} Same table. Two people. Two different slices of it. {{slices}} A grant on a table is all or nothing. So this lesson cuts the table more finely. Privileges go to jobs, not to people. Columns can be granted one by one. A view can hand out an age band and keep the date of birth. {{cuts}} And a policy can decide row by row, from an attribute the person cannot change. {{rows}} Each cut has a way round it. A view runs as its owner. A function can read what its caller cannot. Turning on row security quietly hides everything from anybody with no policy. {{ways}} By the end, the server itself answers who may read what. Not anybody's memory. {{matrix}}
